::: {.why}
The regression you ran last night has a problem you would spot instantly in any other context, and it is the same problem you spend your working life correcting for.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Estimate lambda by regression and say why the estimate is biased.
- Name an instrument or design that would address the bias, and say whether you can implement it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} State the problem precisely: order flow is not exogenous, because traders respond to price moves as well as causing them, so the regression coefficient mixes impact with reaction. This is simultaneity, and you would reach for an instrument immediately in a Mendelian randomization setting.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Try the fixes available to you: estimate lambda separately in periods with different noise trading volume, use lagged rather than contemporaneous flow, and compare against an estimate from the permanent impact of large trades from day 284. Report all three and note the spread between them, which is the honest uncertainty about lambda for your symbol.
:::
:::

## Resources

- [Kyle (1985) — Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading](https://people.duke.edu/~qc2/BA532/1985%20EMA%20Kyle.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}
- [linearmodels — panel, IV/2SLS and Fama-MacBeth (Sheppard)](https://bashtage.github.io/linearmodels/) [tool]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
Three estimates of lambda from different designs with the spread between them reported as the uncertainty.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Your regression of returns on order flow is biased. Say why, and name the design you would use if you could.
:::
